name: Pointillism
means: Colour mixed in the eye: the whole image built from discrete dots of pure hue, no blending, luminous.
tags: pointillism, dots of pure color, optical mixing, luminous, no blending
prose: a pointillist painting built entirely from discrete dots of pure colour, mixing optically, luminous
works_for: video - STILL UNTESTED, and the attempt to test it exposed a bug. The card declares engine=anime while recommending a qwen LoRA (illustration-qwen-image), and workflow 22_anime_kf_ipadapter.json has no LoRA node, so the keyframe rendered as a soft anime illustration with no dot field and the video pass had nothing pointillist to preserve. The clip in samples/video is real but it does not test this style. Fix the engine/LoRA routing first, then re-run. comic_halftone and stop_motion_felt carry the identical mismatch. Note that the neighbouring dot-field prediction it was meant to corroborate - manga_screentone - was measured and FAILED to boil, so the prior behind 'a dot field is the worst case for temporal stability' is now doubtful rather than safe.
note: manga_screentone proved this engine CAN produce a dot field, which is the reason to expect pointillism to work where comic_halftone did not. | Authored in the second wave, after the first 64 were rendered and measured. status=untested because nothing here has been rendered yet - the first wave shipped 46 cards marked ready without a single render and 27 of 64 turned out to be routed to the wrong engine. | ENGINE CORRECTED anime -> qwen: The dot field only resolves with illustration-1.0-qwen-image, which is a qwen LoRA, so the card is routed to qwen. On the illustration engine the dots read as falling snow.
verdict: RESCUED BY A STYLE LoRA. Without one the dots still read as falling snow over a photograph, and at seed 314159 the control has no dots at all. With illustration-1.0-qwen-image the figure is genuinely built from discrete dots of pure colour that mix optically - the coat a dense field of blue, red, yellow, orange and green dots that resolves to dark tweed at a distance, the face pale dots with red gathered into the cheeks and nose, the scarf red and dark-red dots. Verified at four seeds (5150, 7, 99999, 314159) and monotonic in strength: 0.6 speckles a photograph, 0.8 begins building the surface, 1.0 converts coat and scarf, 1.2 converts the whole figure and starts pulling the background off photography, 1.5 leaves the background a grey wash. THE LIMIT, and it is real: the dots stop at the figure's silhouette. The ground is never divisionist, so this is a pointillist SUBJECT rather than a pointillist painting - the same bargain claymation is marked ready on. ROUTING BLOCKER: this card says engine=anime and the LoRA is qwen-based, so the recommendation cannot load until engine is changed to qwen. studio/_tools/lora_rescue.py; studio/samples/lora_rescue/.
verified_by: Looked at, against the no-style control at the same seed with the same subject, on both engines. studio/_tools/style_examples.py --all-engines

video_verdict.failure: the style never rendered - engine/LoRA mismatch
video_verdict.saw: This clip cannot answer the question it was chosen for. The keyframe is not pointillist - it is a soft anime illustration with mild stipple in the background and on the scarf. The card declares engine=anime while recommending the qwen LoRA illustration-qwen-image at 1.2, and the anime keyframe workflow (22_anime_kf_ipadapter.json) has no LoRA node at all, so the LoRA was never applied and the dot field never rendered. The video numbers that came back (detail 1.011, boil 0.147, motion 0.527) describe a soft anime illustration holding steady, which is true and useless. The dot-field prediction stands untested.
video_verdict.measured_on: One 193-frame (8.04s) LTX-2.3 image-to-video clip, workflow 12_ltx23_i2v_audio.json at its shipping settings, from a keyframe rendered on this style's own engine at 1280x704. Held constant across every style in the sweep: subject, keyframe seed 7204, video seed 8801, motion prompt, clip length. MEASURED BY RENDERING AND LOOKING, NOT PREDICTED.
video_verdict.caveats: boil is NOT a style-stability number in this sweep - it tracks how much the clip moved, and the identical motion prompt produced motion from 0.345 to 2.772 across styles. detail is the load-bearing number, and it too drops when the COMPOSITION changes rather than the texture. Read both against the strips. n=1 clip, one subject, one seed.
